## Quality Check of the data

### Analysis setup

A fixed random seed was used to ensure reproducibility, particularly for the doublet-detection step. The data come from the 10X Genomics base.

```{r}
# Define the sample information
sample.name <- "Brain_DV200"
species <- "Human"

# Set a fixed random seed for reproducibility
the.seed <- 42
set.seed(the.seed)

# Load the packages required for quality control and doublet detection
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scDblFinder)
})
```

Dataset from 10x Genomincs : Manual dissection

<https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/7.1.0/4plex_human_lungcancer_glioblastoma_scFFPE_multiplex_Glioblastoma_Manual_BC3/4plex_human_lungcancer_glioblastoma_scFFPE_multiplex_Glioblastoma_Manual_BC3_count_sample_raw_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz>

## Loading the raw count matrix

The dataset corresponds to the manually dissociated glioblastoma sample from the 10x Genomics FFPE multiplex experiment. The raw feature-barcode matrix was used, meaning that it contains both cell-containing droplets and a large number of empty droplets.

```{r}
# Define the path to the raw 10x Genomics feature-barcode matrix
raw_data_path <- "../data/raw_data/sample_raw_feature_bc_matrix"

# Read the sparse count matrix
scmat <- Read10X(
  data.dir = raw_data_path
)

# Verify the structure of the imported object
class(scmat)
dim(scmat)
```

The dimensions of the raw matrix were recorded before filtering.

```{r}
# Record the dimensions of the unfiltered matrix
n_raw_features <- nrow(scmat)
n_raw_barcodes <- ncol(scmat)

cat("Raw features:", n_raw_features, "\n")
cat("Raw barcodes:", n_raw_barcodes, "\n")
```

The raw matrix contained 37 143 features and 392 837 barcodes. At this stage, barcodes should not all be interpreted as cells because the raw matrix includes empty droplets and background RNA.

## Barcode-rank curve

The total number of UMIs was calculated for every barcode. Barcodes were then ranked from the highest to the lowest RNA content to generate a barcode-rank, or knee, plot.

```{r}
# Calculate the total number of UMIs detected in each barcode
nb_umi_by_barcode <- data.frame(barcode = colnames(scmat),nb_umi = Matrix::colSums(scmat))

# Rank barcodes from the highest to the lowest UMI count
nb_umi_by_barcode <- nb_umi_by_barcode %>% arrange(desc(nb_umi)) %>%
  mutate(barcode_rank = seq_len(n()))
```

The barcode-rank curve was used as a diagnostic representation of the transition between RNA-rich droplets and the background population.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot(nb_umi_by_barcode,aes(x = barcode_rank,y = nb_umi)) + 
  geom_point(size = 0.5,alpha = 0.6) +scale_x_log10(name = "Droplet rank (log scale)") +
  scale_y_log10(name = "Number of UMIs per droplet (log scale)") +
  labs(title = paste0("Barcode-rank plot of the ",sample.name," sample")) +theme_classic()
```

The curve displayed a broad transition in the range of a few thousand UMIs. Because the transition was not used as a strict automated cell-calling threshold, subsequent filtering was based on the observed gene, UMI and mitochondrial distributions.

As the raw matrix was used, the initial gene and UMI filters also acted as an empirical empty-droplet filter. A statistical method such as `DropletUtils::emptyDrops()` could be used as a complementary sensitivity analysis, but it was not used to define the primary dataset in this workflow.

By visualization, we take 3000 as the knee of this plot.

## Initial creation of the Seurat object

An initial Seurat object was created by retaining genes detected in at least five barcodes and barcodes containing at least 200 detected genes. This first permissive filtering step removed the lowest-complexity portion of the raw matrix while preserving candidate cells for further inspection

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(SoupX))

# Define candidate cells (barcodes with >= 200 detected genes)
cell_barcodes <- colnames(scmat)[Matrix::colSums(scmat > 0) >= 200]
filt_mat <- scmat[, cell_barcodes]

# Initialize the SoupChannel
sc <- SoupChannel(scmat, filt_mat)

# Perform temporary clustering to identify cell-type specific markers for background estimation
cat("Running temporary clustering for SoupX marker identification...\n")
sobj_temp <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = filt_mat)
sobj_temp <- NormalizeData(sobj_temp, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- FindVariableFeatures(sobj_temp, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- ScaleData(sobj_temp, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- RunPCA(sobj_temp, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- FindNeighbors(sobj_temp, dims = 1:20, verbose = FALSE)
sobj_temp <- FindClusters(sobj_temp, resolution = 0.5, verbose = FALSE)

sc <- setClusters(sc, setNames(sobj_temp$seurat_clusters, colnames(sobj_temp)))

# Estimate the ambient RNA contamination fraction (rho)
sc <- autoEstCont(sc, 
                  tfidfMin = 1.0, 
                  soupQuantile = 0.90, 
                  priorRho = 0.05, 
                  priorRhoStdDev = 0.1)

# Generate the corrected count matrix (integer format for downstream compatibility)
adj_matrix <- adjustCounts(sc, roundToInt = TRUE)

# --- Diagnostic Block: Assess overall ambient RNA removal ---
removed_counts <- filt_mat - adj_matrix

# 1. Calculate global impact
total_original <- sum(filt_mat)
total_removed <- sum(removed_counts)
pct_removed <- round(100 * total_removed / total_original, 2)

cat("--- SoupX Correction Summary ---\n")
cat("Total ambient UMIs removed:", total_removed, sprintf("(%s%% of entire dataset)\n", pct_removed))

# 2. Identify the genes that formed the majority of the "soup"
top_soup_genes <- head(sort(Matrix::rowSums(removed_counts), decreasing = TRUE), 10)
cat("\nTop 10 genes most affected by ambient RNA removal:\n")
print(top_soup_genes)

# Initialize the final Seurat object with the cleaned matrix
sobj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = adj_matrix, 
                           project = sample.name, 
                           min.cells = 5, 
                           min.features = 200)

n_initial_cells <- ncol(sobj)
n_retained_genes <- nrow(sobj)

cat("\nSoupX Correction Complete. Initial candidate barcodes:", n_initial_cells, "\n")

# Free memory 
rm(sobj_temp, sc, filt_mat, scmat, removed_counts, top_soup_genes)
gc()
```

The initial object contained 10 306 candidate barcodes and 18 988 genes.

```{r}
# Inspect the metadata generated by Seurat
head(sobj@meta.data)

# Inspect a small portion of the count matrix using the public accessor
GetAssayData(sobj,assay = "RNA",layer = "counts")[1:5, 1:5]
```

The raw matrix and the barcode-rank table were no longer required after creation of the Seurat object.

```{r}
# Remove large intermediate objects to release memory
rm(nb_umi_by_barcode, scmat)
gc()
```

## Gene complexity assessment

The number of detected genes per barcode was used to identify droplets with insufficient transcriptional complexity. Low complexity barcodes may represent empty droplets, cell debris or severely damaged cells.

```{r}
# Summarise the number of genes detected per candidate barcode
summary(sobj$nFeature_RNA)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5

# Visualise the distribution of detected genes
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(sobj$nFeature_RNA,breaks = 200,xlab = "Number of detected genes",
     main = "Detected genes per barcode")

VlnPlot(sobj,features = "nFeature_RNA",pt.size = 0.01) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 800,colour = "red",linetype = "dashed")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

```

The distribution contained a large population of low-complexity barcodes. A minimum threshold of 800 detected genes was selected from the observed distribution.

No upper gene-count threshold was applied at this stage. Brain and tumour cells can exhibit high transcriptional complexity, and an arbitrary upper cut-off could remove genuine biological populations. Potential multiplets were evaluated later using `scDblFinder`.

## UMI-count assessment

The total UMI count per barcode provides an additional measure of RNA content. Barcodes with very low UMI counts are less likely to contain intact, transcriptionally informative cells.

```{r}
# Summarise the total number of UMIs per candidate barcode
summary(sobj$nCount_RNA)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5

# Visualise the UMI-count distribution on linear and logarithmic scales
VlnPlot(sobj,features = "nCount_RNA",pt.size = 0.01) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1000,colour = "green",linetype = "dashed")

VlnPlot(sobj,features = "nCount_RNA",log = TRUE,pt.size = 0.01) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1000,colour = "green",linetype = "dashed")
```

The relationship between the number of detected genes and the total UMI count was examined to identify the main complexity trend and potential extreme observations.

```{r}
# Calculate the correlation between gene and UMI counts
gene_umi_correlation <- cor(sobj$nFeature_RNA,sobj$nCount_RNA,method = "pearson")
gene_umi_correlation
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6

FeatureScatter(sobj,feature1 = "nCount_RNA",feature2 = "nFeature_RNA",pt.size = 0.1) +
  labs(title = paste0("Gene–UMI relationship (Pearson r = ",round(gene_umi_correlation, 2),
      ")"))
```

The two metrics were positively correlated, as expected for droplets containing increasing amounts of cellular RNA. A minimum threshold of 1,000 UMIs was selected.

## Filtering low-complexity barcodes

Barcodes were retained when they contained more than 800 detected genes and more than 1,000 UMIs.

```{r}
# Define the empirical lower thresholds
minGenes <- 800
minUmi <- 1000

# Retain barcodes satisfying both complexity criteria
sobjFiltrd <- subset(sobj,subset = nFeature_RNA > minGenes &nCount_RNA > minUmi)

# Record the number of candidate cells after gene and UMI filtering
n_after_complexity <- ncol(sobjFiltrd)

cat("Cells after gene and UMI filtering:",n_after_complexity,"\n")
```

The joint gene and UMI filtering retained 4 359 candidate cells.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5

# Inspect the distributions after complexity filtering
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd,features = c("nFeature_RNA","nCount_RNA"),ncol = 2,pt.size = 0.01)

FeatureScatter(sobjFiltrd,feature1 = "nCount_RNA",feature2 = "nFeature_RNA",pt.size = 0.1)
```

The unfiltered Seurat object was removed after the complexity-filtering step.

```{r}
# Remove the initial object to reduce memory usage
rm(sobj)
gc()
```

## Mitochondrial transcript assessment

The proportion of mitochondrial transcripts was calculated using genes beginning with `MT-`. An increased mitochondrial proportion can indicate damaged or dying cells, although the expected distribution depends on the tissue-processing and sequencing protocol.

```{r}
# Calculate the percentage of mitochondrial transcripts in each cell
sobjFiltrd$percent_mt <- PercentageFeatureSet(sobjFiltrd,pattern = "^MT-")

# Summarise the mitochondrial percentage
summary(sobjFiltrd$percent_mt)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5

# Visualise the mitochondrial-percentage distribution
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd,features = "percent_mt",pt.size = 0.01) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10,colour = "red",linetype = "dashed")

ggplot(sobjFiltrd@meta.data,aes(x = percent_mt)) + geom_histogram(bins = 100,colour = "black",
    fill = "grey70") + geom_vline(xintercept = 10,colour = "red",linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Mitochondrial transcript percentage",x = "Mitochondrial transcripts (%)",
    y = "Number of cells") +theme_classic()
```

The relationship between mitochondrial percentage and total UMI count was examined to assess whether mitochondria-enriched cells also tended to have reduced RNA content.

```{r}
# Calculate the correlation between mitochondrial percentage and UMI count
mito_umi_correlation <- cor(sobjFiltrd$percent_mt,sobjFiltrd$nCount_RNA,method = "pearson")
mito_umi_correlation
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4

FeatureScatter(sobjFiltrd,feature1 = "nCount_RNA",feature2 = "percent_mt",pt.size = 0.1) +
  labs(title = paste0("Mitochondrial content and UMI count (Pearson r = ",
                      round(mito_umi_correlation, 2),")"))
```

Most candidate cells had low mitochondrial percentages. A maximum threshold of 10% was selected according to the observed distribution and the FFPE probe-based nature of the dataset.

```{r}
# Define the maximum mitochondrial-percentage threshold
maxpct_mt <- 10

# Remove cells with elevated mitochondrial transcript proportions
sobjFiltrd <- subset(sobjFiltrd,subset = percent_mt < maxpct_mt)

# Record the number of cells after mitochondrial filtering
n_after_mito <- ncol(sobjFiltrd)
n_removed_mito <- n_after_complexity - n_after_mito

cat("Cells after mitochondrial filtering:",n_after_mito,"\n")

cat("Cells removed by mitochondrial filtering:",n_removed_mito,"\n")
```

The mitochondrial filter retained 4 278 cells and removed 81 cells.

## Doublet detection

Droplets containing two or more cells can generate hybrid transcriptional profiles and artificial connections between otherwise distinct populations. Doublets were identified using `scDblFinder`.

The Seurat object was temporarily converted into a `SingleCellExperiment`, which is the input format expected by `scDblFinder`.

```{r}
# Convert the Seurat object into a SingleCellExperiment
sceobj <- as.SingleCellExperiment(sobjFiltrd)

# Reset the seed before the stochastic doublet-detection step
set.seed(the.seed)

# Detect putative doublets
doublet_res <- scDblFinder(sceobj)
```

The predicted doublet classifications were transferred back to the Seurat metadata.

```{r}
# Store the doublet classifications in the Seurat object
sobjFiltrd$doublets.class <- doublet_res$scDblFinder.class

# Display the number and proportion of predicted singlets and doublets
doublet_table <- table(sobjFiltrd$doublets.class)
doublet_proportions <- round(100 * prop.table(doublet_table),1)

doublet_table
doublet_proportions
```

```{r}
# Record the number of predicted doublets
n_doublets <- sum(sobjFiltrd$doublets.class == "doublet")

doublet_percentage <- round(100 * n_doublets / ncol(sobjFiltrd),1)

cat("Predicted doublets:", n_doublets, "\n")
cat("Predicted doublet percentage:", doublet_percentage, "%\n")
```

Predicted doublets were removed before dimensionality reduction and clustering.

```{r}
# Retain only cells classified as singlets
sobjFiltrd <- subset(sobjFiltrd,subset = doublets.class == "singlet")

# Record the final number of retained cells
n_final_cells <- ncol(sobjFiltrd)

cat("Final number of singlets:",n_final_cells,"\n")
```

The intermediate `SingleCellExperiment` objects were removed after doublet detection

```{r}
# Remove intermediate doublet-detection objects
rm(sceobj, doublet_res)
gc()
```

## Final quality-control assessment

The final distributions of detected genes, UMI counts and mitochondrial percentage were inspected after all filtering steps.

```{r}
# Display summary statistics for the final dataset
summary(sobjFiltrd$nFeature_RNA)
summary(sobjFiltrd$nCount_RNA)
summary(sobjFiltrd$percent_mt)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5

# Visualise the final QC distributions
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd,features = c("nFeature_RNA","nCount_RNA","percent_mt"),ncol = 3,
        pt.size = 0.01)
```

A summary table was generated to document the number of barcodes or cells retained at each step of the workflow.

```{r}
# Summarise the number of barcodes or cells retained after each QC step
qc_summary <- data.frame(step = c("Raw barcodes","Initial Seurat filtering",
                                  "Gene and UMI filtering","Mitochondrial filtering",
                                  "Doublet removal"),
                         retained_barcodes_or_cells = c(n_raw_barcodes,n_initial_cells,
                                                        n_after_complexity,
                                                        n_after_mito,n_final_cells))

qc_summary
```

The final dataset contained 3956 predicted singlets and 18 988 retained genes. These cells passed the gene-complexity, UMI-count and mitochondrial-content filters and were not classified as doublets.

## Normalisation

The retained count matrix was normalised using Seurat’s `LogNormalize` method. For each cell, gene counts were divided by the total cellular count, multiplied by the default scale factor of 10,000 and log-transformed.

```{r}
# Normalise gene expression while preserving the raw counts
sobjFiltrd <- NormalizeData(object = sobjFiltrd,normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
  scale.factor = 10000,verbose = FALSE)
```

Raw counts remained available in the `counts` layer, while the normalised expression values were stored in the `data` layer. We can also perform SCTransform, but this method does require some computational ressources since it uses GLMs to adjust residus

```{r}
# Verify the RNA layers present after normalisation
Layers(sobjFiltrd[["RNA"]])
```

## Saving the filtered object

The filtered and normalised Seurat object was saved for the dimensionality-reduction, clustering and annotation analyses.

```{r}
# Define the output path
filtered_output_file <- paste0("../data/processed_data/",sample.name,"_FILTERED.rda")

# Save the filtered and normalised Seurat object
save(sobjFiltrd,file = filtered_output_file)

cat("Filtered object saved to:",filtered_output_file,"\n")
```

The saved object is subsequently loaded by the clustering script.

```{r}
# Record the software versions used in the analysis
sessionInfo()
```
